published_statement: Abstract (p.1): 'We present an approximate time-dependent metric in ingoing Eddington-Finkelstein coordinates for an evaporating nonrotating black hole as a first-order perturbation of the Schwarzschild metric, using the linearized backreaction from a realistic approximation for the stress-energy tensor for the Hawking radiation in the Unruh quantum state.' Sec. II p.8: 'we solve Eq. (53) up to relative corrections of the order of 1/mu^2 in the Planck units'. Eq. (64): f(z) = alpha z^2/(16 pi (1 - z)). Summary (p.21): 'using the linearized backreaction from the stress-energy tensor of the Hawking radiation in the Unruh quantum state in the unperturbed spacetime ... to first order in the stress-energy tensor of the unperturbed Schwarzschild metric. Therefore, our metric should be a very good approximation everywhere near to and everywhere outside the event horizon when the mass is large in Planck units.' Type IV (p.17): 'Numerically we find that the stress-energy tensor for the massless conformal scalar is Type IV everywhere outside the horizon for both of Bardeen's fits [64] and [65] and also for the earlier fit by Visser [21] with k3 = 0. However, for massless spin 1, it is only Type IV for 0 < z < 0.04374 for [64] or for 0 < z < 0.06151 for [65] ... we are not certain that the stress-energy tensor for the electromagnetic field in the Unruh state is Type IV ... anywhere outside a slowly evaporating Schwarzschild black hole.' Read pages report no mass-function sign and no m < 0 anywhere.
published_hypotheses: H1 first-order (linearized) perturbation of Schwarzschild; relative corrections O(1/mu^2) retained, higher orders dropped (p.1, p.8, p.9, p.21)
H2 <T_munu> is evaluated on the UNPERTURBED Schwarzschild background (eq. 31, p.6; 'in the unperturbed spacetime', p.21) -- the source is not iterated to a fixed point
H3 spherically symmetric Unruh state (no incoming radiation at past null infinity or past horizon; regular on the future horizon) (p.1, p.6)

H4 massless fields only; eq. (2) mu' = -alpha/mu^2 with alpha ~ 3.7474e-5 for photons and gravitons, valid 'when the black hole mass mu is much larger than the reciprocal of the masses of all massive particles' (p.2)
H5 mass large in Planck units; metric applies for v << -1 and u < 0 (p.3 Fig. 1 caption, p.21)
H6 slowly evolving metric: orthonormal <T> taken as mu0^-4 x dimensionless functions of z at fixed z (dimensional analysis, eq. 36, p.6)
H7 mass infinite at u -> -infinity (no formation event); for a hole formed at M0 the metric holds for mu(u) < M0 (p.2)

H8 Type-IV conclusion is for the conformally coupled massless scalar, from numerical FITS (Bardeen [64],[65], Visser [21]) to computed stresses; spin 1 undecided, hinging on the disputed asymptotic k3 z^3 transverse-stress term (pp.16-17)
H9 gauge choice g(1) = h(1) = 0 (p.9); trace fixed by the conformal anomaly T(z) = beta xi z^6 (eq. 70), not the full trace for gravitons (p.9)

OUTSIDE THE CANONICAL STATEMENT: selfconsistent.py:26 / index3.py:399 / obstruct.py:145 / paper/CLAIMS.md:119 read APT as 'a Type IV stress-energy DOES source a metric'. At source the Type-IV classification is of the Unruh <T> on the unperturbed Schwarzschild background (H2, eq. 31-36); Martin-Moruno & Visser 2102.13551v2 sec. 2.2.4 file APT under test-field stress-energy tensors. At O(hbar) G^(1) = 8 pi <T>[g0] so the linearized Einstein tensor inherits Type IV -- both readings are consistent with the text; the tree's own 'first order' qualifier (selfconsistent.py:29-33, obstruct.py:145-150) carries it.

rederivation.outcome: All 15 checks PASS (exit 0). (1) eq. (3) solves eq. (2). (2) eq. (4) -> eq. (5) algebra with r = 2mu/z. (3) eq. (9) is the Cardano root of the depressed cubic mu^3 - 3 mu0^2 eps mu - mu0^3 = 0 (residual 8e-51 at 60 digits; a first float run showed 3e-6, which was catastrophic cancellation in MY double-precision evaluation at eps = 1e-6, not a fault in eq. 9). (4) eq. (5) is that cubic. (5) Covariant conservation on Schwarzschild of a pure flux T^r_t = C/r^2 (Christoffels computed). (6) eq. (64) f = alpha z^2/(16 pi (1-z)) re-derived by a DIFFERENT route than APT's 01 Einstein component: conservation + L = alpha/mu^2 at first order. (7-9) The two printed forms of each of eqs. (65), (66), (67) agree. (10) eqs. (49),(51),(52) give trace -rho + P + 2p = T. (11) Hawking-Ellis 2x2 discriminant = (rho+P)^2 - 4f^2, so Type IV iff (rho+P)^2 < 4f^2. (12) Kretschmann = 48 M^2/r^6. (13) eq. (70) spin 0 matches the conformal anomaly. (14) f0 = alpha/(16 pi beta) consistent with L = 16 pi beta f0/mu^2. (15) scope arithmetic: the 1.126e9 kg hole of selfconsistent.py has mu*m_e = 2.17e-6, violating eq. (2)'s hypothesis. Printed xi/96 ratios 7/4, -13, -233/4, 212 match the Christensen-Duff coefficients as recalled (NAMED-NOT-READ). NOT re-derived: g(z), h(z), S(z), the numerical Type-IV claim (needs the unread fit coefficients and eqs. 38-47, 72-93), and any mass-function sign (APT print none on read pages).

Neither refutes the other; the tree's use in throatmass (not static, not m<0) is untouched.

lacked_data: What the authors had: the Unruh-state <T> as numerical fits (Bardeen [64],[65], Visser [21]); the photon+graviton alpha; the conformal anomaly. What came later or stays missing: (a) neutrino masses -- the authors already HAD oscillation evidence and their alpha = 3.7474e-5 is the photon+graviton value, i.e. they incorporated that datum (a 1976-era alpha with massless neutrinos would have been larger); what is still missing is the lightest neutrino mass (could be zero), which would move alpha and hence the luminosity normalisation of f(z), not the time-dependence or any mass sign. (b) the asymptotic k3 1/r^3 transverse stress, which the authors flag as unsettled and which decides spin-1 Type IV only; spin-0 Type IV holds for fits with and without k3 (p.16-17). (c) a beyond-first-order (fixed-point) solution -- a method limit, not a data lack, which the authors state. Evidence either way: none of (a)-(c) changes the facts throatmass.py uses (evaporating, first order in hbar, not static, no m < 0 reported). For selfconsistent.py's separate magnitude use at 1.126e9 kg, the relevant missing ingredient is not later data but the paper's own hypothesis H4 (all massive species frozen out), which fails there by ~6 orders (computed). So M's hypothesis does not bite on this result as throatmass uses it.
grade_evidence: Every fact in the throatmass.py:140-142 row is READ at source: 'evaporating nonrotating black hole' and 'first-order perturbation of the Schwarzschild metric ... linearized backreaction' (abstract p.1; p.8 'relative corrections of the order of 1/mu^2'; p.21), 'time-dependent metric' = not static (abstract; eq. 28 depends on v), is-a-throat False (Schwarzschild perturbation with a horizon), and 'm < 0 reported' False (no mass-function sign and no m < 0 on any of the 11 read pages; a first-order perturbation with O(1/mu^2) relative corrections in its stated domain mu >> 1 cannot flip mu's sign -- a by-hand scope statement, not a computed profile). The sympy re-derivation (15 checks) agrees with every closed form checked, including eq. (64) by an independent conservation route. No moved datum (alpha's neutrino dependence, k3) touches the row. Drift recorded, not repaired: the tree's heading/ledger count APT among 'self-consistent families' (throatmass.py:122, ledger.py:1678, 1729) although APT is a non-iterated linear-response solution outside O5's static class -- the O5 conclusion '0 report m < 0' is identical with denominator 6 or 5. Out-of-scope uses (selfconsistent.py magnitude at 1.126e9 kg dropping H4; the 0.044 quotation) are recorded as drift for their owners and do not bear on this row.
what_would_change_the_grade: (1) An unread page (4-5, 7, 10-15, 18-20) printing a mass function or metric coefficient that goes negative outside the horizon within the stated domain -> would move 'm < 0 reported' and the grade to NARROWED/WRONG for the row; re-read when alphaXiv quota resets. (2) If the grade is taken to cover the tree's classification of APT as a 'self-consistent family' in the fixed-point sense, the right grade for that label is NARROWED (APT: linearized, <T> on unperturbed background). (3) If the grade were extended to selfconsistent.py's magnitude use at 1.126e9 kg, that use is NARROWED (APT eq. 2 hypothesis H4 fails, computed). (4) A later calculation showing the spin-0 Unruh <T> is not Type IV near the horizon would narrow the Type-IV uses elsewhere in the tree, not this row.
